user.text: Create an admin page at /admin that checks if the user has an "admin" role in their session. If the user is not an admin, return a 403 Forbidden response with a nice error page. Use Next.js's built-in auth boundary functions for proper HTTP status codes.

history.assistant:
I added the /admin page. When I tested it, a non-admin user got a real HTTP 403 with a styled error page.

What I changed:
- next.config.ts: turned on experimental.authInterrupts. The forbidden() and unauthorized() functions only work with this setting on.
- app/admin/page.tsx: a server component that calls verifyAdmin() from app/lib/auth.ts. If there's no session it calls unauthorized() (401). If the user isn't an admin it calls forbidden() (403). Otherwise it shows the dashboard with the user's name. The check runs before anything is sent, which is what lets the real status code go out. If you later wrap the page in loading.tsx or <Suspense>, it would return 200 instead.
- app/forbidden.tsx and app/unauthorized.tsx: the 403 and 401 error pages, both built on a shared card in app/components/ErrorPage.tsx with the code, a message and a "Return home" link.

Verification:
- npx next build passed with exit code 0, including TypeScript, and the build output listed authInterrupts as enabled.
- Against next start, curl /admin returned admin=403. The page contained "Access denied" and a noindex robots meta tag, which Next adds automatically.
- / still returned 200.

The mock getSession() always returns a regular user, so I didn't test the admin view. Because the session is hardcoded, Next builds /admin as a static page ahead of time. Once getSession() reads real cookies or headers, the page will be checked on every request.
